criterion: Interface controls on the entry, reel and project states composite directly onto the rendered scene with the scene visible around each control.
evaluation_rule: The controls in question are the WORK and CONTACT capsule at the top right, the list of five links beginning with an arrow on the opening screen, and the title block of an open project. Answer yes when the moving three-dimensional scene shows around and through each of them, with at most a slight blur. Answer no when any of them sits on a solid filled box that hides the scene.

criterion: The chrome capsule glow on the project view takes a warm colour on the Rally project and a cool colour on the E.D.E.N. project.
evaluation_rule: The chrome capsule is the pill holding WORK and CONTACT. Open Rally at its project address, then E.D.E.N. Yes if the soft halo around that pill leans warm on Rally and cool on E.D.E.N.; no if the halo is one fixed colour on both, or absent on both.

criterion: An error on the enquiry form of the contact page appears as near-white words on a darkened band.
evaluation_rule: Submit the enquiry form on the contact page with the name left empty. The verdict is yes when the refusal appears as near-white lettering over a strip slightly darker than the scene behind it, and no when the refusal is set in red lettering or on a red ground.

criterion: Opening the Rally project from the reel of work retints the rendered environment toward a warm amber before the Rally copy appears.
evaluation_rule: The reel of work is the list of project rows reached from the opening screen. Select the Rally row and watch the change. Say yes if the environment behind the interface warms toward amber and the colour arrives ahead of the Rally title and metadata line. Say no if the environment keeps the dark blue of the opening screen, or the copy lands first and the colour follows.

criterion: The studio mark at the centre of the entry state appears as a lit three-dimensional ring with cyan, magenta and amber moving across one polished surface.
evaluation_rule: The entry state is the opening screen that asks What are you looking for?, and the studio mark is the object at its centre. Yes when that object is a shaded ring form turning in light with cyan, magenta and amber sliding across its surface; no when the mark is a flat drawing, a single colour, or missing.

criterion: Pointing at a row on the reel of work brings that title to full strength with every other row dimmed.
evaluation_rule: On the list of project rows, hover the pointer over one title. A yes means the hovered title stays bright while the other rows visibly fade back. A no means hovering changes nothing, or the hovered row is the one that fades.

criterion: A cold load of the entry page shows a field of forward slashes resolving into digits beside a counter before the question appears.
evaluation_rule: Load the site root fresh and watch the first seconds. Yes if the first thing shown is a round block of slash characters filling with digits while a small counter such as /30 climbs, with the question What are you looking for? arriving only afterwards. No if a spinner or a blank black screen comes first, or the question is visible from the start.

criterion: Every interface label across the entry, reel and project states is set in one monospaced typeface rendered in capitals.
evaluation_rule: Compare the arrow links on the opening screen, the project titles in the list, a metadata line such as 2014 / Nimbus / installation, and the WORK and CONTACT capsule. Answer yes when all of them share one fixed-width typeface shown in capital letters. Answer no when two typefaces appear, or any of those labels shows mixed case.

criterion: The project title, metadata line, description and close control on a project view sit together in the lower left eighth of the frame.
evaluation_rule: Open a project such as Rally at desktop width. The judgement is yes when its title, metadata line, description and the Close control are grouped in the bottom left corner region, leaving the rest of the frame to the scene; it is no when that copy is centred, spread across the frame, or held in a side column.

criterion: Moving from the entry state into the reel of work travels on a curve that moves most at the start and settles slowly.
evaluation_rule: From the opening screen asking What are you looking for?, press the SCROLL DOWN control and watch the change into the list of projects. Yes if the movement starts fast and then eases into place over a long, slow settle. No if the change is an instant cut or runs at one even speed from start to finish.

criterion: Tabbing through the entry state shows a teal focus ring offset from each focused control.
evaluation_rule: On the opening screen press Tab several times. Say yes when each control reached shows a teal outline drawn a small gap outside its edge; say no when focus looks the same as hover, or shows nothing at all.

criterion: Asking the assistant on the contact page shows three dots pulsing in turn until the first words of the answer render.
evaluation_rule: The assistant is the input reading ASK ME ANYTHING... on the contact page. Send a question and watch the panel. Yes when three dots pulse one after another from the moment of sending and give way as soon as answer text starts to appear; no when a spinner shows, the dots stay after text arrives, or the answer lands all at once with no indicator.

criterion: Form fields on the sign in page are drawn as single underlines under the label.
evaluation_rule: Look at the Email and Password fields on the sign in page. The answer is yes when each shows its label above a single thin underline with nothing boxing the input, and no when either field is drawn as an outlined or filled rectangle.

criterion: Interface text keeps one near-white on the warm Rally project and on the cool E.D.E.N. project.
evaluation_rule: Open Rally, then E.D.E.N., and compare the lettering of the project copy. A yes means the copy stays the same near-white on both while only the environment behind it changes colour. A no means the lettering itself takes on a warm tint on one project or a cool tint on the other.
